notice: ADJUDICATED CANDIDATE. All 33 anchors were re-examined from primary sources by two independent evidence passes (historians a and b, docs/time/evidence) and an adjudicator (docs/time/ANCHORS-FINAL.md). Anchors are state 'reviewed' (or 'contested' where the sources disagree); none is 'signed': no human historian or the owner has signed the release. Every event time is an estimate with an uncertainty; a clock whose uncertainty exceeds 20 minutes is printed with 'about'.
tz_note: Local mean time at Gettysburg (39.83 N, 77.23 W). 1863 had no standard time zones. EST would be about +9 minutes.

solar.source: NOAA solar algorithm computed by the time-facts specialist for 39.8309 N, 77.2311 W, local mean time; re-derived in tests/time/solar.test.mjs (+-2 min). Not checked against an almanac.

adjudication.by: adjudicator (AI), second reviewer under the unanimity rule, acting on docs/decisions/OWNER-DECISIONS-2026-10-05.md item 2

statuses.Documented: a first-hand primary source gives a clock time for this event or its direct precursor and the window is bounded by sources
statuses.Estimated: no source clocks the event itself; the time is inferred from sequence, neighbouring clocks or astronomy and is labelled an estimate
statuses.Contested: first-hand sources disagree by more than the window an ordinary watch error explains; the range is shown and the status is Contested

adjudication.uncertainty_rule: sigma_min is the half-width of the window the sources defend (rounded up to 5 minutes; the model's own measure). uncertainty_min is the larger distance from the anchor time to either end of that window, rounded up to 5 minutes: a true bound, also for lopsided windows (design anchors: 30). Witness watches in 1863 were not synchronised and the reports show 10 to 30 minutes of scatter, so no event anchor claims better than 25 minutes.
adjudication.about_policy: A displayed clock is prefixed with 'about' when its uncertainty bound exceeds 20 minutes (approx_sigma_min 20). The bound at a tick between two anchors is the linear interpolation of their uncertainties.
